children: Surging energy prices drove up inflation in September, with gasoline accounting for more than half of the monthly rise in the U.S. Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Wednesday.

Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% from the prior month, faster than August's 3.9% increase and up 34% over the past year, while other motor fuels, which include diesel, soared 15.3% on the month and were 74% higher Y/Y.

The price of unleaded gasoline, which most consumers use at the pump, has climbed 45% since late February, when the U.S. and Israel launched the Iran war, and the price of diesel has surged 70% during the same period.
Airfares, which are highly sensitive to fuel costs, were up 22% from a year earlier, according to the BLS.
Electricity prices also continued to rise in September, ticking up 0.2% for the month and 4.4% for the year.

Some economists said the latest report is a worrying sign that the Iran war is not just a one-off price shock and that higher inflation is here to stay unless the Federal Reserve raises rates more aggressively.

next year.

11.1M barrels last week, which would comprise the biggest drop since June 2025 if confirmed by official data on Thursday.
Front-month Nymex crude
for November delivery rose for the fifth straight session, up 1% to $95.09/bbl, its highest settlement value since September 21, and front-month Brent crude
for December delivery added 0.3% to $106.06/bbl.
Front-month Nymex ULSD (HO1:COM) for November delivery ticked down 0.1% to $4.9274/gal, but front-month Nymex November RBOB gasoline (XB1:COM) gained 0.3% to $3.2595/gal.

gave back most of the previous day's gains, with the front-month Nymex November contract sliding 2.6% to $3.198/gal.

title: Surging gasoline prices accounted for more than half of last month's jump in U.S. inflation
